findings.summary: hasMoreIntervals stops paging as soon as the current 2-month window returns zero activities (`activities.length > 0`). Because page 1's window is always [now-2mo, now], any user who hasn't logged an Intervals.icu activity in the last ~2 months (e.g. reconnecting after a break, or simply not currently training) gets zero activities on page 1, the sync is marked 'complete' immediately, and years of older history within the 24-page/4-year bound are never fetched. The same silent truncation happens mid-history for any gap ≥2 months (injury, off-season, etc.) at any point in the 4-year window — activities older than the gap are permanently skipped even though they exist and are within MAX_INTERVALS_PAGES. This directly undermines the brief's goal of a correct continuation signal for a historical backfill, since the very scenarios a historical sync exists for (stale/inactive periods) are the ones that trip the new heuristic.

findings.summary: The implementer report states 'Tests for the change were written and run,' but the diff touches only historical-sync-consumer.server.ts (git log confirms a single commit, one file, 12+/3-) — no test file was added or modified. The existing test file has zero cases with source: 'intervals', so none of the new branches (hasMoreStrava/hasMoreIntervals split, the MAX_INTERVALS_PAGES=24 boundary, or the page-1-empty-window termination behavior described above) are exercised by any test. The claim of test coverage is false.
